CLAIM_LOCATORS.LOCATOR: All three pages; Figure 1 and task/trait definitions
CLAIM_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Specialisation and communication can create bottlenecks; task parallelism changes whether larger teams help.

EVIDENCE_LIMITS: Rule-based kitchen agent simulation, not a production LLM or human organisation study. Three-page report lacks a full replication protocol; communication restrictions can sometimes reduce redundant coalition formation.

sources.TITLE: Byzantine Fault Tolerance in Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems
sources.AUTHORS_OR_ORGANISATION: Koji Noshiro; Koji Hasebe

CLAIM_LOCATORS.LOCATOR: FT-DCOP model; Theorem 4.2; §5 replication and Proposition 5.1; §6 evaluation
CLAIM_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Fault-tolerant optimisation requires knowledge/replica assumptions; Repl-Max-Sum aims to preserve fault-free Max-Sum behaviour, not make approximate Max-Sum universally optimal.

EVIDENCE_LIMITS: At most k faulty replicas per relevant set and at least 2k+1 knowledge/replica coverage are material; communication multiplication is O(k²) per original message. Main paper inspected; supplementary impossibility proof not independently checked. Synthetic experiments do not certify arbitrary Byzantine MAS.

sources.TITLE: Evaluating XAI Support From A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Policy in Human-Agent Collaboration
sources.AUTHORS_OR_ORGANISATION: Mateus Levi Simões Fernandes; Alberto Sardinha
sources.VERSION_OR_EDITION: AAMAS 2026 extended abstract, 3259–3261; study ethics approval dated 2025-06-11

CLAIM_LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §2 methodology and §3 preliminary findings, pp. 3259–3260; Figure 2 page image inspected
CLAIM_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Triggered status explanations were compared with no explanation in a human–agent Overcooked task; the study did not establish a performance benefit.

EVIDENCE_LIMITS: 38 analysed participants from 41 convenience recruits; control/text/audio groups 14/14/10, four 80-second sessions on one layout, gaming-experienced sample. Underpowered and non-significant results do not establish equivalence or no benefit in all populations. Exploratory adaptation patterns are not confirmed effects.

sources.TITLE: Modelling dialogues using argumentation
sources.AUTHORS_OR_ORGANISATION: Leila Amgoud; Nicolas Maudet; Simon Parsons
sources.VERSION_OR_EDITION: ICMAS 2000, pp. 31–38; inspected author manuscript paginated 1–8

CLAIM_LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §2, manuscript pp.1–2
CLAIM_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Explicitly states inspiration from Dung, adds preferences, and defines acceptable arguments.

CLAIM_LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§3–4, manuscript pp.2–6; p.4 and p.6 images inspected
CLAIM_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Couples argument reasoning to assertion, acceptance, challenge and question moves and public commitment-store updates. Private rationality preconditions remain.

CLAIM_LOCATORS.LOCATOR: End of §4.3, manuscript p.6; §5 and conclusion, pp.6–8
CLAIM_LOCATORS.CLAIM: The syntax alone permits repeated or infinite exchanges; relevance and useful stopping are assumptions left for fuller formalisation. Negotiation/deliberation and multiparty extension are not fully furnished by the basic model.

EVIDENCE_LIMITS: The basic model is two-party, assumes static agreed preference strata and omits retraction. Selected definitions, protocol rules and stated proof results were inspected; predecessor proofs cited elsewhere were not independently checked. No comparative or deployment-effect evidence. Public dialogue commitments are not automatically promises about external task completion.
sources.INSPECTION_NOTE: Actual body §§2–6, relevant definitions/moves, limitations and reference list inspected. ICMAS venue pagination additionally confirmed in EMAS-S056 references. The printed p.6 sentence about truth contains an apparent omitted negation; no quotation or guarantee is inferred from that sentence.

sources.TITLE: Dialogue Games in Multi-Agent Systems
sources.AUTHORS_OR_ORGANISATION: Peter McBurney; Simon Parsons
sources.VERSION_OR_EDITION: Informal Logic 22(3), pp.257–274; issue date as printed, not digitisation date

CLAIM_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Separates dialogue rule types and kinds of commitment; documents the two-party protocol, absent withdrawal and extensions needed for negotiation.
Distinguishes public from private axiomatic semantics and the difficulty of checking an opaque participant’s internal conformance.
Treats termination, complexity, automatability and protocol equivalence as distinct questions. The review’s 2002 research-frontier statements are not present-day status claims.

EVIDENCE_LIMITS: Used for its authors’ methodological distinctions and criticism; origin claims are traced to the inspected EMAS-S055 and EMAS-S031 rather than accepting a review as proof of all cited work. No independent empirical replication. Author overlap with EMAS-S055 is explicit.
sources.INSPECTION_NOTE: Cover, §§4–6 and pertinent references inspected. Does not establish current protocol superiority, contemporary implementation status or the complete primary history of philosophical dialogue games.
